events.t: LIVE — FCC Covered List now bars foreign-produced robots (Jul 28, 2026)
events.why: Adopted, not proposed. Any ground-moving device over 4.4lb (with dock) that senses, connects and navigates cannot get FCC equipment authorisation unless the Department of War grants a Conditional Approval. Read the carve-outs before pricing it: industrial robotic ARMS, medical robots, vehicles and drones are explicitly excluded, so Fanuc, Yaskawa, ABB, KUKA/Midea, Estun and Doosan's cobots are untouched. What is caught is humanoids, quadrupeds and autonomous mobile robots — 9880.HK UBTech head-on, 277810.KQ Rainbow Robotics and TER's MiR unit on the same terms despite being allied, plus 1810.HK Xiaomi's consumer line. HSAI is hit second-hand through its customers' US market access. The asymmetry is the point: US-produced humanoids get a market cleared by rule, everyone else queues for a discretionary exemption.

events.t: Chinese WFE tools qualifying at Samsung and SK Hynix
events.why: Reuters, Aug 4 2026: both Korean memory makers have been testing AMEC etch tools for their China fabs — begun ~2 years ago, aimed at SERVICING and upgrading existing lines rather than adding capacity, after Washington revoked their validated-end-user status in 2025 and replaced it with an annual licence. Small in units, large in meaning: qualification is the slow half of the WFE moat, and it is being done by the two customers whose sign-off other buyers copy. Deutsche Bank has NAURA, AMEC, Piotech and ACM Research each clearing $1B of revenue in 2026 and together taking 25-30% of China's ~$28B WFE market. This is the external bear case (see Thesis) arriving as an event rather than an opinion — watch whether qualification stays confined to China fabs.

events.t: The materials leg under every 'Western winner' still runs through China
events.why: Worth holding against any policy-beneficiary trade in this map. OPTICS: every transceiver laser is built on an indium phosphide substrate, InP has been under Chinese export control since 2025, and it has no substitute at these speeds. Lumentum's CEO has called the InP shortage worse than the memory crunch; AXTI's backlog is >$100M into 2027, and AXTI itself produces in China under the same permit system. The May-Jun 2026 permit easing was selective and politically contingent, not structural. ROBOTICS: a US-built humanoid still needs NdFeB magnets, and the truce covering them expires Nov 10 2026. So a name can win the market-access argument by rule and still lose the input argument by permit. Raw-material depth lives in the Hard Assets sibling map — what belongs here is the conclusion: onshored assembly does not equal an onshored supply chain.
Renewal = status quo; lapse = magnets/Ga/Ge/chemicals shock into robotics, optics and fab chemicals. The single most dated policy risk on the board.

events.t: FCC optical-module ban — the scope question is the whole trade (drafting)
events.why: Chinese vendors hold >50% of the global datacenter-transceiver market, InnoLight alone ~27% (Counterpoint); estimates of the supply cut run to 60%. The consensus trade is to buy the Western replacements — COHR, LITE, AAOI, FN, CIEN, NOK, MTSI, SMTC. Do not take that trade on the headline, because the draft has not resolved the one question that decides it: does the rule follow the COMPANY or the COUNTRY OF MANUFACTURE? Cignal AI, Aug 2026: 'unknown'. If it follows the company, InnoLight routes around it — it is already building in Thailand and Indonesia and sells non-Chinese output under the TeraHop brand — and the ban is largely cosmetic. If it follows the place of production, which is the test the FCC used for robots and inverters on Jul 28, then the replacements are caught too: Coherent manufactures in China, and Lumentum's North American assembly is ramping in THAILAND, as is Fabrinet's entire model. The only listed capacity that clears an origin test outright is AAOI's Sugar Land and Pearland build-out, live from summer 2026 — and Cignal judges AAOI too small to fill the gap. Both branches therefore end in shortage and cost inflation for the hyperscalers rather than clean substitution. Second-guessing the scope is the highest-value work on this lever; the beneficiary list is worthless until it resolves.
